slides.texte_overlay:
Things you should stop doing
as a friend
Stop only texting when you need something. A lift, a favor, a place to crash. Send a message for no reason sometimes. "How did the interview go?" Friends notice who checks in and who only asks.
Stop cancelling at the last minute. Once is life. Every time is a pattern. If you said yes, show up, even for an hour. Reliability is the most underrated thing a friend can offer.
Stop making every story about you. A friend shares news, and you jump in with your own. Let them finish. Ask one more question. "Wait, then what happened?" It's the easiest gift you can give.
Stop roasting friends in front of people they want to impress. Jokes among the boys are fine. In front of his date or his boss, protect him. Good friends make you look good, not small.
Stop keeping score. Who paid last time, who invited who, who texted first. Real friendships aren't fifty-fifty every week. Give a little more than you take and you'll never be short of friends.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. You'll show up with better stories and better questions. Good friends keep growing, not just keep showing up.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. You'll show up with better stories and better questions. Good friends keep growing.

slides.texte_overlay: Stop disappearing when they're going through something. A breakup, a job loss, a sick parent. You don't need the perfect words. "I'm here, want to grab food?" is enough. Just show up.
